title: Complete Guide to Tor & Dark Web Privacy
metaDescription: Learn how to use Tor browser safely for anonymous browsing and dark web access. Setup guide, safety tips, and best practices for maximum privacy.
intro: Tor (The Onion Router) enables anonymous internet browsing through encrypted layers of routing. This comprehensive guide covers safe Tor setup, dark web navigation, and privacy best practices for journalists, activists, and privacy-conscious users.
prerequisites: Willingness to accept slower browsing speeds

steps.title: Download and Install Tor Browser
steps.description: Start by obtaining the official Tor browser from the verified source to ensure you're getting the legitimate, unmodified version.
actions: Visit torproject.org from your regular browser
Click 'Download Tor Browser' and select your operating system
Verify the download signature if possible
Install the browser following the setup wizard
Do not modify default settings during installation
steps.proTip: Always download Tor from the official website. Third-party sources may contain malware or surveillance modifications.
steps.warning: Never download Tor from unofficial sources or torrent sites as these versions may be compromised.

steps.title: Configure Initial Security Settings
steps.description: Tor browser comes with built-in security levels that you should configure based on your privacy needs and threat model.
actions: Open Tor browser and wait for it to connect
Click the shield icon in the top-right corner
Select 'Advanced Security Settings'
Choose 'Safer' or 'Safest' security level
Review and understand what each level blocks
steps.proTip: Start with 'Safer' mode as 'Safest' can break many websites. You can always increase security later.
steps.warning: Changing security settings to lower levels reduces your anonymity protection.

steps.title: Set Up Tor Bridges (If Needed)
steps.description: If Tor is blocked in your country or network, bridges help you connect by disguising your Tor traffic as regular web traffic.
actions: Click on Tor settings before connecting
Select 'Tor is censored in my country'
Choose 'Request a bridge from torproject.org'
Select obfs4 transport type (most reliable)
Copy and paste the provided bridge addresses
steps.proTip: Keep several bridge addresses as backups. Bridges can be detected and blocked over time.
steps.warning: Using bridges may slow your connection further but is necessary in censored regions.

steps.title: Practice Safe Browsing Habits
steps.description: Your browsing behavior is crucial for maintaining anonymity. Small mistakes can compromise your privacy even when using Tor.
actions: Never log into personal accounts while using Tor
Don't download files or enable plugins
Avoid entering personal information on any sites
Use HTTPS versions of websites when available
Don't add extensions or change advanced settings: every change makes Tor Browser easier to tell apart from other Tor users
steps.proTip: Treat every Tor session as if someone is watching. Assume any identifying information can be linked back to you.

steps.title: Navigate the Dark Web Safely
steps.description: The dark web contains both legitimate privacy tools and illegal content. Learn to navigate safely while avoiding dangerous areas.
actions: Start with known safe .onion sites like DuckDuckGo's
Take addresses from the operator's own published page, then check them character by character
Never trust links from unknown sources
Avoid marketplaces and illegal content: many are scams, and marketplaces are regularly seized and run on by law enforcement
Use New Identity when you move between unrelated sites
steps.warning: Many dark web sites contain illegal content or scams. Accessing illegal content can have serious legal consequences.

steps.title: Understand Exit Node Risks
steps.description: Exit nodes are the final relay in the Tor network and can potentially monitor your unencrypted traffic to regular websites.
actions: Always use HTTPS websites to encrypt exit node traffic
Avoid sensitive activities that require login credentials
Prefer a site's .onion address where it publishes one: that traffic never leaves the Tor network through an exit relay
Monitor for unusual behavior or security warnings
Understand that exit nodes can see unencrypted data
steps.proTip: Only unencrypted traffic to ordinary websites passes an exit relay in the clear. A site's .onion address avoids exit relays entirely, and HTTPS-Only mode, on by default, keeps the rest encrypted.

steps.title: Maintain Operational Security (OpSec)
steps.description: Long-term privacy requires consistent security practices beyond just using Tor browser.
actions: Use Tor from a dedicated computer or USB drive when possible
Never mix Tor and regular browsing activities
Keep regular and anonymous identities completely separate
Use different writing styles and habits when anonymous
Consider physical security of your devices
steps.proTip: Create separate 'personas' for different activities. Never let your anonymous and real identities overlap.

pro_tips: Don't add a VPN to Tor expecting more anonymity: the Tor Project doesn't recommend it unless you're an advanced user who can configure both without compromising your privacy.
Use Tails OS for maximum anonymity - it routes all traffic through Tor and leaves no traces on your computer
Disable JavaScript and plugins completely if maximum security is needed, even though this breaks many websites
Save Tor Browser for what needs anonymity and use your everyday browser for signed-in accounts and routine browsing: Tor is slower, and signing in to real accounts over Tor ties that session to you
Create a realistic threat model before using Tor - understand what you're protecting against and adjust your security accordingly

faqs.question: Is using Tor browser legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, Tor is legal in most countries and was originally developed by the U.S. Navy. However, some countries restrict or ban its use, and accessing illegal content through Tor remains illegal.

faqs.question: How slow is Tor compared to regular browsing?
faqs.answer: Tor is noticeably slower than regular browsing because your traffic is relayed through several volunteer machines, often on other continents. How much slower varies with the circuit you get and the time of day.

faqs.question: Can my ISP see that I'm using Tor?
faqs.answer: Yes, your ISP can see that you're connecting to the Tor network, but they cannot see what websites you visit or your activities. Use bridges if you want to hide Tor usage from your ISP.

faqs.question: Is the dark web only used for illegal activities?
faqs.answer: No, the dark web hosts many legitimate services including secure communication tools, privacy-focused search engines, and platforms for free speech in censored countries.

faqs.question: Should I use a VPN with Tor?
faqs.answer: For most people, no. The Tor Project says it doesn't recommend using a VPN with Tor unless you're an advanced user who knows how to configure both in a way that doesn't compromise your privacy: done wrong it reduces anonymity or breaks Tor's protections. To hide from your ISP that you're using Tor, use a bridge instead.

faqs.question: Can government agencies track Tor users?
faqs.answer: While Tor provides strong anonymity, sophisticated adversaries with significant resources may be able to de-anonymize users through various techniques. Perfect anonymity is extremely difficult to achieve.
